how this works

your life vision board is a place for the few things you want your life to add up to, a direction, not a to-do list.

it starts with ten quiet minutes: a handful of honest written answers, which Coach reads to suggest a small set of long-arc goals across six areas of life. you approve, reword, or reject everything, nothing lands on the board without you.

each goal carries a quarterly goal and a little recurring weekly work, deliberately budgeted under the hours you actually have. A two-minute check-in each week keeps it honest, and a deeper look each quarter decides what changes.

common questions
what should I write on the first page?

it's a journal entry, the raw material for everything that follows, so the more honest it is, the more the goals will actually be yours. ramble freely, touch the four things listed under the page, and talk instead of typing if that's easier.

do I have to take the test?

no. "add a goal" works any time, and "add it exactly as written" is always there, your own goal is yours to file, no analysis required. the test just gives the board a considered starting point most people can't write cold.

what does Coach do to a goal I add?

it shapes your words into a workable goal, a title, an honest timescale, a first quarter, and holds up a mirror where it collides with what's already on the board. it also checks the little things: whether the category you picked really fits, and whether the timescale in your words was respected. every change is shown to you, and you can keep your own wording with one click.

why did it reword my goal about winning?

when a goal hangs on something you can't fully control, winning, being chosen, someone else's decision, Coach offers the controllable version and says so in one honest line. the thing you're really after stays in the goal as the aspiration. it's an offer, never a swap: "Keep my wording" is right there.

what's the difference between pausing a goal and deleting it?

pausing is sequencing, not giving up, a paused goal stays on the board, visibly resting, and comes back up at your quarter review. deleting is permanent: the goal and its whole plan go. the board asks twice before it lets you delete.

why can only six goals be active?

because most people move faster on fewer. six is the cap on active commitments, paused goals and dreams are uncapped, so the board never says no to a goal. A full board just makes you choose what rests first.

what are habits and tasks?

the weekly work that actually moves a goal, habits that happen on a rhythm, one-time tasks, capabilities that build. they're deliberately budgeted under your available hours, so one bad week doesn't end the whole thing.

what are the check-ins?

weekly: about two minutes, how did each area of life feel, one optional honest line. A rough week may gently shrink a goal's weekly work; a good one may raise it a notch, always with your say-so. quarterly: the deeper look, progress, tensions you chose to hold, and what leads next quarter.

my goal has a deadline a few weeks away, does it fit here?

yes, at its honest length. a short push is offered as this quarter's focus under the goal it serves, or stands on its own measured in weeks. it's never stretched into years to fit the board.

where does my writing go? is it private?

your answers live in this browser (and in your account, when you're signed in, so they follow you across devices). they're sent to the AI only to run the analysis you asked for. everything you type is saved as you type it, so a closed tab or a failed call never loses your words.

do I need the internet for this?

for the analysis, yes, and when it can't run, the app says so and stops rather than guessing. there's no canned fallback pretending to know you. adding your own goals as written always works.

can I change my name?

click your name in the big title, it edits in place. Enter saves, Escape puts it back.
